newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Bunds to eke out few more gains to 101.25.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bunds to eke out few more gains to 101.25.

text.p: June Bund futures on LIFFE are likely to extend Tuesday's strong gains and aim for 101.25 on Wednesday, dealers and analysts said.

"What we saw yesterday, because of the figures, was a very strong strong short squeeze," said a dealer at a German bank in Frankfurt. "The opening shows we will still have upside potential -- 101.25 is the target today."

June Bunds on the DTB at 0624 GMT were at 101.13, up 0.13 from Tuesday. LIFFE June Bunds ended on Tuesday at 100.97. The 101.25 level was the low on March 7 and the area around there and the March 14 low of 101.19 has capped the market.
Lower-than-expected U.S. employment cost figures on Tuesday propelled bond markets higher, although U.S. Treasuries strongly outperformed their European counterparts.

The German bank dealer said Bund trade would be muted, with a holiday in Germany on Thursday, apprehension about Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls on Friday and a holiday in London on Monday all giving players a reason to keep a low profile.
"We saw the biggest move yesterday," he said, but he added that sentiment would remain positive.
He pegged support near 100.94, an area which he said marked the top of a prior range between there and the 100.30 region.

Tim Hampton, futures salesman at Royal Bank of Scotland in London, said Bunds were entering a new trading period where cautious buying on dips was recommended. He said 100.75-66 was key support as the 38.2 percent and 50 percent retracement points of the move from 100.28 on April 25.

"Once this area has been confirmed as support, build longs through 101.19 over coming days as Bunds take on the direction hinted at by the continuation in the flattening of the Euromark strip," he said.
June Euromarks were up 0.01 at 96.76. All the 1997 futures were up 0.01, while all four 1998 contracts were up 0.02.
